What are methods of providing RF high availability?
Full overlapping coverage provides an alternate AP path if a radio or AP fails, supporting RF availability at the cost of additional infrastructure and careful channel planning.
What two 802.11 amendments deal with regulatory and transmission requirements?

The supplied key lists 802.11d and 802.11f. 802.11d addresses regulatory-domain operation, but 802.11h is the amendment associated with DFS and transmit-power control in 5 GHz. The listed 802.11f appears inconsistent with the question; verify this item before relying on its answer key.

When performing an indoor predictive site survey to make the WLAN planning and design cycle more efficient, what is a best practice for configuration of the simulated APs in the predictive modeling software?
Always use the default 2.2 dBi omnidirectional antenna patterns for simulated APs.
If dynamic RRM will be used, AP transmit power should be set to an estimated average level of the expected client devices, such as 25 mW.
All simulated APs should be set to 20 MHz channels only.
Defining custom AP and antenna patterns will yield more accurate prediction data than the preconfigured vendor AP/antenna combinations.

When dynamic RRM will control transmit power, simulated AP power should represent a realistic average client/AP environment. That makes the predictive model a more useful starting point for the eventual RRM-managed WLAN.
What are the three biggest WLAN enterprise verticals?(Choose all that apply.)
Education, healthcare, and retail are major enterprise WLAN verticals because each commonly relies on pervasive wireless connectivity for core operations.
Using a SCA means that all APs will be using the same channel in a given layer. How is the AP with which the client associates determined?
All APs share a virtual Multicast Address. A controller will tell the closest AP to the client to communicate with it, since it has a greater RSSI from the client.
All APs share a virtual BSSID. A controller will tell the closest AP to the client to communicate with it, since it has a greater RSSI from the client.
All APs share a virtual IP address. A controller will tell the closest AP to the client to communicate with it, since it has a greater RSSI from the client.
The client selects the AP based on a known set of MAC to BSSID mappings stored in the clients authorized SSID listing.

In a single-channel architecture, the controller/client uses stored mappings between the authorized SSID and AP BSSIDs to identify the AP to associate with, rather than selecting solely by a conventional per-AP channel scan.
When live video streaming solutions that transmit simultaneously to more than one recipient are used, what special capability should be considered and configured in all affected WLAN implementations?
Multicast lets one sender distribute the same stream to multiple receivers without creating a separate full-rate stream for each client.
Excessive uplink RTP frame retransmissions can result in ____________.
Deauthentication of the transmitter by the receiver
Lowering of the data transmission rate by the transmitting station
Repeated uplink RTP retransmissions consume airtime and indicate poor link quality. Rate adaptation can lower the transmitting station's PHY rate to improve reliability.
What part of the 802.11n preamble is used by the receiver to estimate the spatially multiplexed signal channel? What mode is this used in?
HT-LTF in Mixed and Greenfield modes
HT-STF in Mixed and Greenfield modes
The HT-LTF fields in the 802.11n preamble let the receiver estimate the MIMO channel for spatially multiplexed streams. They are present in both HT mixed and HT greenfield formats.

A signal passes through a 10-meter cable, an amplifier, and then a filter. The amplifier has an output that is eight times higher in power than its input. Each meter of cable reduces the signal level by a factor of 4. The filter has a loss of 5 dB. What is the total loss/gain of the three elements in series?
The cascade must be analyzed in dB: cable loss, amplifier gain, and filter loss add algebraically. The stated components produce the net loss identified by the answer key.
Which operational plane would be responsible for performing automated RF management?
The control plane coordinates WLAN behavior, including automated RF management such as channel and transmit-power decisions.
When selecting a centralized WLAN architecture, what new problem may arise when you change the data forwarding model from centralized to distributed?
Centralized control functions, such as key management and distribution, RRM, and load balancing will no longer be supported.
The router between the APs and the controller must be made aware of the APs as forwarding client STAs.
APs that were designed for a centralized forwarding model may not support all features in distributed forwarding mode.
All RRM controls will also need to be distributed to a master AP that acts as a channel and transmit power arbiter for other APs in the ESS.
Distributed forwarding can expose capability gaps: an AP designed primarily for centralized forwarding may not implement every feature required when client traffic is switched locally.
To increase capacity in a coverage-based wireless network, which of the following techniques are typically recommended?(Choose all that apply.)
Maximize airtime usage by disabling lower data rates.
Add additional APs and use directional antennas.
Turn up power on the access points.
Lower power on the access points and, after careful planning, add more AP
Capacity-based design increases usable airtime: remove unnecessary low data rates, add APs where demand requires them, use directional antennas to control cells, and tune power to improve reuse.
HR/DSSS specifies the following PHY rates:
HR/DSSS defines the legacy 802.11b data rates: 1, 2, 5.5, and 11 Mbps.
Location technology (RTLS) can use which of the following methods?(Choose all that apply.)

RTLS can use several technologies, including acoustic, Wi-Fi, active RFID, and infrared methods. The source answer key lists these four; other technologies such as UWB are also used in some RTLS systems.

You have been tasked with performing safety and operations training for outdoor bridge link installation. The antennas are to be installed on a 70-foot tower on one end and the roof top of an office building on the other end. What might be required for the tower installation?
Special antennas that avoid reflections on the tower poles.
APs that are designed to operate above 70 feet.
Special RF cables that will not create loss incurred by the metal tower construction.

Tower poles and nearby metal can reflect RF energy and distort the antenna pattern. Use an antenna/mounting arrangement designed to minimize those reflections and maintain the intended radiation pattern.
During a customer walkthrough you notice an area of the CAD drawing where it is not accurate. What next step should you take?
Redraw the portions of the map that have changed.
Request the survey team to do their best to walk where necessary and use the references on the map.
An inaccurate CAD floor plan undermines scale, AP placement, and propagation modeling. Obtain a corrected drawing before continuing the design.
iPerf is a tool used in site surveys and validation surveys for what purpose?
iPerf generates TCP or UDP traffic between endpoints to measure achievable network throughput under controlled conditions.

You are configuring an 802.11ac AP using manual channel planning. The design specification calls for the current AP to be placed on channel 56 in 5 GHz and to disable the 2.4 GHz radio. For what could the 2.4 GHz radio be used if not standard AP operations?
Some APs can repurpose a 2.4 GHz radio for Bluetooth services such as scanning or location functions while the 5 GHz radio carries the WLAN. This depends on the AP's supported radio modes.

Given: As the wireless network administrator for XYZ Company, you are planning to upgrade your aging wireless network infrastructure, as well as some clients, to support 802.11ac. In your research, you have discovered that your new wireless client devices and infrastructure are 802.11ac, WMM, and WMM-PS certified by the Wi-Fi Alliance. Some of your existing client devices are 802.11a/b/g devices that do not support WMM. Given this information, what scenario is possible when your company's employees begin using both types of client devices on the new WLAN?
All WMM-PS certified client devices will be prevented from utilizing WMM-PS features until all stations in use on the wireless medium are WMM-PS certified.
Performance and battery life will be inconsistent between WMM-PS and non-WMM-PS client devices when used with applications that support WMM-PS.
The WLAN infrastructure will set the dozing times of the WMM-PS certified client devices based upon their WMM access category, while the non-WMM-PS client devices will continue to use PSPoll frames.
WMM-PS enabled APs will allow both WMM-PS and non-WMM-PS stations to use the triggeranddelivery mechanism, but WMM-PS stations will g

WMM Power Save behavior depends on client support. WMM-PS clients can use trigger/delivery mechanisms, while legacy non-WMM clients use different power-save behavior, producing inconsistent performance and battery life.
When analyzing published competitive tests by equipment vendors, what items are the tests usually lacking?(Choose all that apply.)
Detailed configurations of each vendors equipment
Vendor competitive tests are difficult to compare without client models/configurations, repeatable test methodology, and detailed equipment configurations.
